title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine responsible for sinking Russian warship in Libya – Europe live
summary: President says Kyiv responsible for sinking Merkury warship in Benghazi on Sunday and also drone attack on cargo vessel MV Angara

blocks.text: Morning opening: Ukraine claims responsibility for sinking Russian warship in Libya

Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy has claimed responsibility for sinking a Russian warship at a Libyan naval base on Sunday, saying it was part of Kyiv’s response to Russia’s continuing aggression.

blocks.caption: Acombination of satellite images shows a Russian corvette and the northern port area before (above) and after (below) an explosion aboard a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi naval base, Libya. Photograph: VANTOR/Reuters

blocks.text: “An exemplary Ukrainian operation in response to Russia’s war,” he said in a post on X, with a video showing the moment the corvette was hit by Ukrainian drones.

“Our warriors deployed seven Ukrainian-made naval drones. Despite all the enemy’s efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk. It’s one of their newest ships, commissioned in 2023, during the full-scale war,” he said.
Zelenskyy added that a Russian dry cargo vessel MV Angara, which he said was used for transporting weapons, was also sunk.
Elsewhere, Nato and the UN will meet today to discuss the security situation in the region.

Nato’s North Atlantic Council (NAC) will meet to discuss the events of last Friday, when three Russian missiles crashed in Poland amid a broader assault on Ukraine. Poland is expected to ask for further military support from allies.
And the UN security council will meet to discuss Russian attacks on civilian targets, including the consulates of Austria and the Netherlands in Kyiv.
I will bring you all the latest here.
It’s Monday, 23 November 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.
